results.title: NKX2-1-Related Disorders - GeneReviews® - NCBI Bookshelf
results.content: _NKX2-1_-related disorders range from benign hereditary chorea (BHC) to choreoathetosis, congenital hypothyroidism, and neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (also known as brain-lung-thyroid syndrome). The diagnosis of an _NKX2-1_-related disorder **is established** in a proband with suggestive findings and a heterozygous pathogenic (or likely pathogenic) variant in _NKX2-1_ identified by molecular genetic testing [Inzelberg et al 2011] (see Table 1). Several large contiguous deletions have been identified in individuals with clinical features of _NKX2-_ 1-related disorders, including an individual with choreiform movements, neonatal respiratory distress, and hypothyroidism and a 3.5-Mb deletion adjacent to but not interrupting _NKX2-1_ [Barnett et al 2012]. _NKX2-1_-related disorders include benign hereditary chorea (BHC) and choreoathetosis, congenital hypothyroidism, and neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (collectively known as brain-lung-thyroid syndrome). The broad phenotypic spectrum associated with pathogenic variants in _NKX2-1_ (including BHC and a variable combination of lung, thyroid, and neurologic abnormalities) led [Willemsen et al [2005]](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK185066#) to coin the term "brain-lung-thyroid syndrome." Considering the variable manifestations of individuals with pathogenic variants in _NKX2-1_, the authors suggest that these disorders be referred to as _NKX2-1_-related disorders.
